name: Mellin transform
ant_definition: For a suitable weight w:(0,infinity)->C, M[w](s)=integral_0^infinity w(u)u^(s-1)du on its fundamental strip.
equivalences: after u=e^y, Mellin transform becomes a two-sided Laplace/Fourier-type transform in log scale
examples: compactly supported smooth weights give rapidly decaying Mellin transforms on vertical lines
counterexamples: an arbitrary nonsmooth or slowly decaying weight need not have a Mellin transform on the desired strip
formal inversion without integrability and contour hypotheses is unauthorized
pvg_translation: The factor w(n/x) weights decoded valuation points by multiplicative scale. It is global in n and not a coordinatewise local axis operator.
loses: individual point recovery after aggregation unless the full family of transforms is retained

name: weighted Mellin inversion route
formula: sum_n a(n)w(n/x) = (1/(2*pi*i)) integral_(c-i*infinity)^(c+i*infinity) F(s) M[w](s) x^s ds
hypotheses: c in a common valid strip
counterexample: The displayed integral is not authorized merely because F and M[w] are written formally.

name: smoothing kernel
definition: A weight replacing a sharp cutoff 1_{n<=x} by w(n/x), typically with compact support or controlled decay and regularity.
counterexamples: a discontinuous sharp cutoff has weaker transform decay
smoothing does not by itself improve an arithmetic theorem without coefficient or analytic input

name: regularity-decay ledger
rules: more differentiability plus endpoint control generally yields more vertical decay after integration by parts
compact support alone does not guarantee arbitrary decay without smoothness
a jump produces only polynomially limited decay
decay claims require explicit derivative and boundary hypotheses

name: exponential smoothing
preservation: all coefficients contribute with exponentially decreasing scale weight

name: von Mangoldt exponential observable
claim_ceiling: formal/known transform route only; no PNT conclusion
pvg_translation: single-axis prime-power points weighted by log(p) and then by exp(-decode(alpha)/x)

name: smoothing is not a proof engine
false_inference: rapid decay of M[w](sigma+it) implies PNT or a zero-free region
rejection: Kernel decay controls the test-function side; it does not supply nonvanishing or bounds for zeta or L-functions.

questions: What is the Mellin transform of the supported built-in weight?
